description_text:
Product Manager Intern 
Internship Duration: 3 or 6 months 
Remote · India

About the role
We are a small founding team building a cloud-based SaaS platform and looking for a motivated Product Manager Intern to learn and contribute alongside our product lead. This is a hands-on internship. You will work on real product documentation, real workflow analysis, and real functional specifications that directly influence what gets built.

What you will do?
Analyze software products and document how they work; every screen, every step, every user action, every possible outcome.
Write functional requirement documents that describe exactly what a feature should do so engineers can build it without needing clarification.
Map complete user workflows from start to finish; what the user sees, what they click, what happens next, and what happens when something goes wrong.
Create workflow diagrams and flowcharts that make complex processes easy to understand for both technical and non-technical team members.
Research how similar products handle specific features and document your findings clearly.
Write test cases for each feature; what should work, what should not work, and what edge cases need to be checked.
Identify missing features or workflow gaps and document them with a clear description of the problem and a suggested solution.
Participate in product discussions and contribute observations about how features could be improved or simplified.

Skills required
Structured thinking. You can take a complex process and break it down into clear logical steps. You notice when something is missing or does not make sense.
Written communication. You can write clearly and precisely. Someone reading your document should understand exactly what you mean without needing to ask follow-up questions.
Attention to detail. You notice inconsistencies. You catch edge cases. You read things carefully before accepting them as correct.
Basic understanding of how software products work. You know what a user flow is, what a requirement document looks like, and what the difference between a feature and a bug is.
Familiarity with documentation tools. Google Docs, Notion, or similar. You can create structured documents, diagrams, and organised notes.
Currently pursuing or recently completed any degree in Engineering, Business, or a related field.

Nice to have
Any exposure to product management concepts such as user stories, acceptance criteria, and functional specifications.
Experience using or studying any software product deeply enough to explain how it works end to end.
Familiarity with flowchart or diagram tools such as Figma, Miro, Lucidchart, or draw.io.
A portfolio, Notion page, or document showing how you have analysed or documented something even informally.
Participated in a case competition, product hackathon, or similar event.

What you will gain?
Hands-on experience working on a real product being built from scratch.
Direct mentorship from the product lead who will review your work and explain the reasoning behind every decision.
Deep understanding of how SaaS products are designed, documented, and built end to end.
A real portfolio of product analysis and documentation work you can show in any future interview.
Potential for a full-time Product Manager role based on performance.

Availability
We are looking for someone who can join immediately or within one week of offer acceptance. Please apply only if you are available to start within this timeframe.

description_text:
BuzzBoard

Remote (WFH)
Product

About BuzzBoard

BuzzBoard builds AI products for the B2SMB market — helping agencies, media companies, and sellers understand small businesses and market to them at a level of personalization that wasn't previously economical.

Our platform is built on frontier models end to end. Not AI features bolted onto a legacy product — the products are agent systems.

Our products span multi-agent marketing content generation, real-time AI voice intake, and pre- and post-sales intelligence for SMBs — Zylo, IRIS, Ignite, and Ember. They share a common internal pipeline for orchestration, retrieval, tool use, evaluation, and deployment, and a spec-driven development process that treats agent behavior as a first-class design artifact.

The role

This is a Product Manager role for people who build, not just specify.

Two things are equally true about how we work, and both are non-negotiable expectations of this role:

The products you own are agent systems, and they are non-deterministic. Your design surface is prompts, tool definitions, retrieval strategy, schema contracts, model selection, fallback behavior, and failure modes. “The model got it wrong” is a product bug you are expected to diagnose and specify a fix for — not escalate
You use these models to do the product work. You will write specs, generate structured data, produce working HTML prototypes, run evaluation batches, and analyze output quality using the same models the products run on. Our specs ship as machine-readable handoff sets, and prototypes ship with live model stubs. If your definition of a spec is a Confluence page of prose, this role will be uncomfortable

What You'll Actually Do

Own one or more product lines — outcomes, roadmap, sequencing, and the quality bar
Write the spec set engineering builds from: product spec, engineering spec, model spec, and handoff readiness — decisions resolved, not deferred
Design the agent behavior — prompt architecture, output schemas, deterministic vs. model-decided logic, guardrails, and what happens when the model is wrong or the tool call fails
Build prototypes yourself — working HTML with live model calls, ahead of engineering commitment, so we argue about a thing instead of a document
Define and run evaluations — build eval sets, score output batches, set ship/no-ship thresholds, and drive prompt and model iteration off measured results rather than vibes
Make the model tradeoffs — model choice, context strategy, latency, token cost per unit of output, fine-tune vs. prompt vs. retrieval
Work directly with engineering, GenAI, and design on daily execution; hold the line on schema and interface contracts between agents
Interface with customers and enterprise partners, including US-based partners with real security, privacy, and compliance review processes
Instrument and read the data — usage, quality, cost, and drift — and act on it

What we're looking for

Required

4+ years in product management, ideally B2B SaaS
Demonstrated hands-on work with LLM / agent products: prompt design, structured output, retrieval, tool/function calling, evaluation. We will ask you to walk through something you shipped in detail
Fluency using AI tooling in your own workflow — specs, prototypes, analysis, code reading
Ability to read code and API contracts well enough to review a schema, follow a pipeline, and spot a bad interface
Track record of shipping — features live, in customers' hands, with measured outcomes
Strong written communication; you can take a technical decision and make it legible to a CEO and to an engineer in the same document
Comfort operating with ambiguity and short cycles

Preferred

Degree in AI/ML, Engineering, CS, or a related technical field
Direct experience with OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Anthropic/Claude, LangChain, or equivalent orchestration stacks
Experience with voice AI, agentic workflows, or multi-agent systems
Experience with fine-tuning, dataset curation, or model performance analysis
Experience working with US customers and enterprise partners
SMB or marketing-technology domain knowledge

What this role is not

Not a backlog-grooming or ticket-triage role
Not a role where AI strategy is delegated to a data science team you email
Not a role where a spec can end with “TBD, engineering to decide”

What we offer

Fully remote
Genuine ownership of a product line, with the latitude to shape it
Work at the current frontier of applied AI product development — agent systems, evals, voice, and multi-model orchestration in production
A small, high-context team that moves quickly and argues about the work
Real impact on the small businesses our customers serve

Apply if you're a product manager who builds with these models daily and wants to own products made of them.

title: Senior Product Manager - AI Learning & Games
ai_core_responsibilities: Lead the product vision for AI-powered learning tools, integrating learning science and game design to create impactful educational experiences. Collaborate with AI/ML engineers to build voice-first tutors and adaptive assessments for first-generation learners in low-connectivity contexts.
ai_requirements_summary: Requires 5-8 years of product experience and a proven track record of shipping at least one actual game. Candidates must demonstrate deep knowledge of learning science and hands-on proficiency with AI/LLM prototyping tools.
description_text:
Senior Product Manager - AI Learning & Games

NavGurukul · AI Learning Labs

📍 Remote (India / Diaspora) · 30% travel · Full-time
⏱ 5–8 Years of Experience

The brief

Here is the design problem we are trying to solve.
A Class 9 student in rural Muzaffarpur has intermittent internet, a low-end Android device, limited English, and has never had a teacher who had time to explain the same concept three different ways. She is not a struggling learner. She is a learner who was never given the right tools.

Now imagine building an AI-powered learning experience for her, one that feels less like a textbook and more like a game she wants to come back to. One that speaks her language, literally and figuratively. One that adapts to how she thinks, not how a standardised curriculum assumes she should think. One that works offline, on her phone, without a cloud subscription.

The danger we are designing against is real: it is entirely possible to build something engaging that teaches nothing. A game that holds attention but does not build understanding. An AI tutor that feels helpful but does not change what a learner can actually do. We are not building for engagement. We are building for learning, and that distinction is everything.
That is what we are building. And we need someone who has actually shipped a game, understands learning science, and can hold both without letting either one compromise the other.

What we are building and why

Join us in building AI-powered learning for India at scale.
Imagine a future where India’s 248 million students have access to personalised learning experiences tailored to how they learn, not how a standardised curriculum assumes they should. Government platforms like DIKSHA, UPI, and Aadhaar have shown us that transformative technology can reach national scale when built with intention and adopted by the state. The opportunity to do this for learning is vast, and it is happening now.

But here is the catch: learning is not like UPI. A transaction works the same way whether you are in Delhi or Dharwad. Learning, though, is radically different. A Class 9 student grasping algebra needs something entirely different from someone learning music, from an adult upskilling, from a rural learner in Muzaffarpur with intermittent connectivity. No single application solves this. The education system has known this for decades and done almost nothing about it.

So we are taking a different approach: building focused, context-specific applications, each pedagogically grounded and proven to deliver real impact before we scale. A tool for foundational maths. One for vocational skills. One designed around how a first-generation learner actually engages. AI is what makes this feasible at pace, it personalises within each context and dramatically shortens our development cycles.
This is Bharat tech at its finest: problem-first, people-centred, and built for the billions.

What this role is

We are looking for a Senior Product Manager who sits at the intersection of three things: learning science, game design, and AI. Not someone who dabbles in all three, someone who holds all three as serious disciplines and knows how to make them work together.

Learning science is the non-negotiable. Every product decision, how a concept is introduced, when feedback is given, how difficulty scales, what a learner does when they are stuck must be grounded in how people actually learn. Game design and AI are the tools we use to make that learning rigorous, accessible, and genuinely engaging for learners who have never had a product built for them. The sequence matters: learning outcomes first, everything else in service of that.

AI/ML is the engine of everything we build. You do not need to train models. You do need to prototype with AI tools, deeply understand what LLMs and voice models can and cannot do, and make product decisions grounded in how the technology actually behaves, not how a demo makes it look.
You will shape the product vision for our AI learning tools, voice-first tutors, game-based skill builders, adaptive assessments, AI interviewers working within priorities set at the org level and collaborating closely with AI/ML engineers, learning designers, and leadership. You will own the how: the experience, the interaction design, the quality of what ships, and the learning outcomes it drives.
This is a senior individual contributor role. The right person grows into Head of Product as the team scales.

What you will be doing

Shape the product vision for NavGurukul’s AI learning tools to bring learner insight, learning science, and game design thinking into every conversation about what gets built and how.
Hold learning outcomes as the non-negotiable constraint. Every design decision, loop structure, feedback timing, difficulty progression, and interaction model gets evaluated first by whether it serves learning, then by whether it is engaging.
Apply game design thinking in service of learning science: core loop design, progression systems, mastery arcs, and the feeling of genuine improvement, not engagement for its own sake.
Work with AI/ML engineers to define what the AI needs to do to support real learning, Socratic questioning, adaptive difficulty, contextual feedback and specify that clearly enough that engineers can build it.
Prototype with AI: use LLM APIs, voice tools, and no-code/low-code AI tooling to sketch interactions quickly, test learning hypotheses, and validate ideas before engineering commits to them.
Design for the constraint: offline-first, voice-first, low-end devices, vernacular languages. The constraint is not the problem; it is the design brief.
Run user research with first-generation learners in low-literacy, low-connectivity contexts. Let that research reshape the product, not just validate it.
Define and track learning outcome metrics, mastery, confidence, retention, transfer, and build the measurement framework to know whether what we shipped actually worked.
Write crisp, unambiguous specs that engineers and learning designers can both act on.

What we are looking for

Two hard filters: please read both
First: you must have shipped at least one game. Not a gamified feature. Not points and badges bolted onto an existing product. An actual game, with a core loop, progression, and players who chose to keep playing. It does not have to be a commercial hit. It has to be real.
Second: you must be able to talk about that game or any product you have built in terms of what people learned or got better at, not just how long they stayed. If your instinct is to lead with retention and DAUs rather than learning gain and skill transfer, this is probably not the right role. We care deeply about engagement, but only because engagement is what makes learning possible, not as an end in itself.
If you have not shipped a game, or if learning outcomes have not been central to how you think about product success, this role is not the right fit. We have other product roles that may be.

Beyond that, we are looking for
5–8 years of product experience, with a clear arc from shipping to influencing product direction in collaboration with leadership.
Genuine familiarity with learning science, spaced repetition, retrieval practice, worked examples, cognitive load, and formative feedback. You do not need a PhD, but you need to have engaged with this seriously.
Comfort working in an environment where strategic priorities are set at the org level, and the value you add is depth of craft, learner insight, and execution quality.
Hands-on comfort with AI tools: you prototype with LLM APIs, you have built something with voice or conversational AI, you know where the seams are between what AI can do reliably and where it falls apart.
Experience designing for voice-first or conversational interactions, you think naturally in flows that do not start with a text field or a screen tap.
User research experience in non-standard contexts, you know how to get a signal from users who are not used to giving structured feedback.
Clear, sharp communication, a one-pager from you should align engineers, learning designers, and leadership in the same room.

Bonus
Formal or self-directed study in learning science, cognitive psychology, instructional design, or education research.
Prior experience in EdTech or learning science-informed products.
Familiarity with vernacular-language or low-resource user contexts Tier 2/3/4 India, low-literacy users, first-generation learners.
Experience working at or with a nonprofit, social enterprise, or mission-driven startup.

Why join NavGurukul?

A design brief that does not exist anywhere else: learning science as the foundation, game design and AI as the tools, and learners who have never had a product built for them as the audience.
Ownership of the craft, the experience, the interaction design, the learning outcomes. You are the person who makes sure what ships actually work.
AI as your core building material, not a feature you are adding, but the foundation of everything you ship.
A place to belong: paid Vipassana breaks, 26 paid learning Saturdays a year, and a community that genuinely invests in your growth.
A clear path to Head of Product as the team and impact scale.
Purpose Over Pay, As a nonprofit, our salaries are below corporate benchmarks. But what we offer in return is immense purpose, autonomy, and the chance to work with passionate, mission-driven people.

When you apply, tell us

Tell us about the game you shipped. What was the core loop? What kept players coming back? And critically, what did players learn or get better at, and how did you know?
Describe a product decision you made that was grounded in learning science. What principle were you applying, and what was the outcome?
Describe a time you used AI tools to prototype or validate a product idea. What did you build and what did you learn?
What draws you to this role specifically, at this point in your life?
How soon can you join if selected?
Let’s build the future of learning, together. ♥

description_text:
About The Role

We're a Webflow design and development agency serving B2B and SaaS clients. Our delivery stack runs on a no-code foundation — Webflow, Airtable, Softr, Xano, Memberstack, n8n — and we're increasingly layering AI into everything we do, with Claude as our primary tool.

We're hiring someone who blends Business/Product Analyst and Product Manager DNA — sitting at the intersection of strategy, design, and engineering. You'll take vague client problems and drive them through discovery, wireframing, documentation, build coordination, and launch. On the PM side, you'll think in roadmaps, prioritize ruthlessly, define what success looks like, and own outcomes — not just outputs. This applies to both client projects and our own internal products.

This is not a role for someone learning the ropes. We need 3+ years of real BA, PM, or equivalent experience — you've scoped projects, written PRDs and SRS documents, run UAT, prioritized backlogs, handled stakeholders, and shipped things that went live.

What You'll Do

Discovery & Client Strategy

Run discovery calls with clients. Translate business problems into clear scope, constraints, and dependencies.
Write approach documents, SRS, formal proposals, and budget reports.
Own stakeholder engagement and solution evaluation end-to-end.
Bid on RFPs — craft well-scoped, compelling responses.

Product Management

Own product strategy and roadmap for both client builds and our internal products.
Write PRDs, define MVP scope, and prioritize features against business goals — not just feature requests.
Define success metrics for what you ship and follow up to see if they were hit.
Run customer feedback loops: synthesize user interviews, support tickets, analytics into clear product decisions.
Maintain backlogs. Run sprint planning. Make hard calls on what doesn't get built.
Conduct competitive analysis and market research to inform positioning and feature decisions.

Design & UX

Sketch UX wireframes for Webflow designs and internal tool builds.
Drive user-centred design (UCD): user research, personas, user flows, journey maps, information architecture.
Prototype in Figma, Whimsical, Miro — whatever gets the idea across fastest.
Run user testing before shipping.

Documentation & Delivery

Write user stories, flow charts, and UML diagrams that the dev team can build from without needing clarification.
Coordinate with developers to ensure specs are understood and the build matches the intent.
Run UAT. Maintain BA artefacts. Keep project documentation accurate and current.

Systems & AI

Use Claude daily as a working collaborator — for drafting specs, generating user stories, analyzing feedback, writing proposals, and automating repetitive work.
Design and build internal systems: Airtable bases, Claude-powered workflows (MCP, Claude in Chrome, Cowork, Claude Code), automation pipelines that connect our stack.
Treat repetitive tasks as automation candidates. If you did it twice, the third time should be a system.
Research emerging no-code and AI tools, pilot the ones that matter, drop the ones that don't.

Required

3+ years of experience as a Business Analyst, Product Manager, Solutions Architect, or equivalent role. Freshers will not be considered.
Product thinking. You've owned a product or feature end-to-end — not just gathered requirements. You can defend why something should or shouldn't ship, and you measure outcomes after launch.
Communication: 8/10 or better. This role is customer-facing. You write clean emails, run discovery calls without rambling, and explain technical tradeoffs to non-technical founders.
Hands-on experience with Claude or similar AI tools. Not surface-level use — you've built workflows, used Projects, and ideally touched MCP, Claude Code, or comparable agent tooling. If you can't show us how you've used AI to actually do work, this isn't the role for you.
Systems thinking. You see patterns, build repeatable processes, and document what you figure out.
No-code fluency. Working knowledge of at least 2–3 of: Webflow, Airtable, Softr, Xano, Memberstack, n8n, Zapier, Figma.
UX fundamentals. You can wireframe. You understand IA, user flows, UCD. You've shipped real products.
Documentation discipline. PRDs, user stories, SRS, approach docs, proposals — writing is a core deliverable, not an afterthought.

Preferred

Prior experience as a PM at a SaaS company or as a BA/PM at a digital agency.
Experience bidding on and winning RFPs.
Background with SaaS or B2B clients.
Familiarity with SEO, analytics (GA4, GSC), or growth tooling.

How You'll Know You're a Fit

You read a client brief and your first instinct is "what's the cleanest system to solve this."
You'd rather spend an afternoon teaching Claude to do a task than doing it manually 20 times.
You enjoy both the strategy (why are we building this?) and the detail (why is this button on the left?).
You work well asynchronously, write clearly, and don't need to be chased for updates.

Logistics

Experience: 3+ years (strict)
Shift: 7:00 PM – 4:00 AM IST (US overlap hours)
Location: Remote, India-based

How To Apply

Send us:

Your CV with clear mention of relevant experience.
One short paragraph on how you've used Claude or other AI tools to actually do work — what you built, automated, or systematized.
A link or brief description of something you've shipped, written, wireframed, or documented.

description_text:
About BJAK
The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role
BJAK is building a Neobank Superapp for Southeast Asia. As a Technical Product Manager, you’ll own a product vertical end to end—such as payments and expense management, remittance, insurance, or wealth and trading—from strategy, outcomes, and roadmap through to the technical design and delivery of the systems behind it.

This is a product where real money moves, mistakes are immediately visible, and licensing, compliance, and third-party rails are core product constraints—not considerations around the edges.
We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal. The bar is knowing where a model can genuinely improve an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted when money is involved.

What you'll be doing
Own a vertical end-to-end — outcomes and metrics, a backlog prioritised by value / risk / dependency / strategic priority, acceptance criteria crisp enough to build and test against.
Shape the technical design with engineering — system boundaries, money-movement correctness (idempotency, ledgering, reconciliation), third-party-rail reliance and rail-down behaviour, failure/retry/refund paths, security, latency, scalability, recovery.
Make hard trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability and UX — and defend them to an engineering, compliance or ops lead who pushes back.
Treat regulated constraints as first-class product inputs — licensing scope, CDD/KYC and limits, sanctions/PEP screening, transaction monitoring, data residency and privacy. Know which are hard launch gates and which are forward-readiness.
Apply AI where it earns its place — define what it's allowed to decide, where a human stays in the loop, how it's evaluated, and what it does when unsure. Every AI-surfaced number traces back to a real record.
Ship against external gates — build feature-complete behind flags; go live per rail as each partner and regulatory gate clears.
Work across Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance/Reconciliation.

What you'll need
Product leadership — significant experience owning a complex technical product end-to-end; strong judgement and decisiveness under ambiguity; ability to balance ambition against technical, regulatory and operational reality; can hold their own with senior engineers.
Technical foundation — solid system design (boundaries, datastores, queues/workflows, APIs, failure modes, consistency under concurrency); comfort reading, reviewing and challenging design docs; can sketch an architecture and a sequence. No production code, but technical enough that engineers don't have to simplify.
Domain — experience in a regulated / high-consequence domain (payments, banking, remittance, insurance, …) or demonstrable fast-ramp ability; understands why money movement is different (correctness over convenience, irreversible states, partners you don't control).
AI judgement — hands-on with LLM-based products; can frame a feature as eval-able (offline, online, human feedback); realistic on hallucination/drift/data gaps, including data-blocked vs model-blocked and when a model must not be in the loop at all.
Nice to have — engineer or highly-technical-PM background · zero-to-one · shipped AI-heavy consumer products · defined eval metrics for ML/LLM systems · AI UX + failure-handling intuition · SEA market experience.

Outcomes
Clear vertical strategy and legible roadmap
Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch
Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds
AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted
Trade-offs made deliberately under uncertainty and hold up when challenged
Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction

Location
This role is remote, but candidates must be based in India. We are hiring specifically for this market, so applicants should already be based in India.

Language
English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.
Interview Process
Our process is designed to move fast:
1. Online assessment or practical task
2. Role-specific interview
3. CEO / final round
For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

description_text:
About BJAK
The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role
We are looking for product managers to own product areas within BJAK's AI Neobank app.

This role is for builders who can understand users, define product direction, work with engineering and design, launch fast and keep improving after release.
What You'll Own
Own product areas across insurance, payments, savings, investing, travel or other financial services.
Define user problems, product scope, success metrics, roadmap and launch plans.
Work with engineering, design, data, operations, compliance and business teams.
Turn complex financial products into simple, usable customer journeys.
Use data, feedback, research and production issues to improve product decisions.
Launch features, monitor performance and drive iterations.
Make trade-offs between speed, user experience, business impact, compliance and operational complexity.
What We're Looking For
Experience as Product Manager, Product Owner, founder, growth/product operator or similar role.
Strong product sense and ability to simplify complex workflows.
Able to work with engineers and designers to ship real products.
Comfortable with metrics, user feedback, experiments and post-launch learning.
Strong writing, prioritization and stakeholder management.
High ownership and ability to drive work with limited guidance.
Experience in fintech, insurance, payments, consumer apps or high-growth products is a strong advantage.
The Kind of Builder We Want
Starts from user problems, not feature lists.
Can make decisions with incomplete information.
Knows how to ship quickly and learn after launch.
Works well with engineering without hiding behind process.
Honest about what changed because of their work versus wider team effort.
This Role Is Not For
People who only write decks and do not drive execution.
PMs who cannot work deeply with engineering.
Candidates who need perfect data before making decisions.
People who launch features and then stop caring.
PMs who exaggerate business impact without understanding attribution.
Location
This role is remote, but candidates must be based in India. We are hiring specifically for this market, so applicants should already be based in India.
Language
English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process
Our process is designed to move fast:

Online assessment or practical task
Role-specific interview
CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

description_text:
Who are we?

Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Description

About the Role

We're looking for a Senior/Staff Product Manager to join our Data & Analytics team and own the product strategy for data platforms, analytics tooling, and AI-driven capabilities. This role sits at the intersection of data engineering, business strategy, and applied AI — you'll translate complex business needs into a clear product roadmap, while working hand-in-hand with data engineers to ship scalable, reliable, and high-impact solutions.

This is a high-visibility, cross-functional role for someone who can operate at both strategic and technical depth, partner effectively with engineering and business stakeholders, and has hands-on experience shipping AI/ML-powered products.

What You'll Do

Product Management for Data, BI and AI product

Manage and execute the data analytics product vision to help business teams adopt data and use it confidently for decision-making.

Lead end-to-end delivery of AI-powered analytics products — from problem framing and data feasibility assessment through model evaluation, deployment, and adoption.
Define success metrics, build business cases, and prioritize a roadmap balancing technical debt, platform scalability, and business impact.
Provide statistical techniques, quantitative data analysis, predictive analytics, and scenario-based analysis to support product decisions.

Cross-Functional Partnership

Engage with cross-functional business and IT teams to understand requirements, analyze, design, and help build solutions for analytics and data science products.
Partner closely with Data Engineering to design scalable data pipelines, infrastructure, and platform capabilities that support analytics and AI use cases.
Work directly with business partners (Sales, Marketing, Customer Success...) to identify high-value problems, gather requirements, and translate them into actionable product specs.
Collaborate closely with analysts and data scientists across the organization, including on model development, evaluation, and responsible AI practices (bias, explainability, governance).
Analyze complex requirements and translate them into simple, actionable user stories.
Maintain deep knowledge of cross-functional data and ensure data quality on all products launched.

Delivery & Execution

Build dashboard prototypes to help business stakeholders visualize end products.
Get involved in testing analytic products for functionality, user interface, and data quality.
Provide technical support to business teams for self-serve analytics; define best practices and develop user guides.
Follow agile methodologies and deliver continuous enhancements to products.
Optimize release management to strike the right balance between business goals and delivery capacity.
Identify and manage risks in release delivery and communicate clearly with stakeholders, including mitigation plans.
Debug and identify root causes for critical issues and provide solution recommendations.
Ensure data security and compliance measures are in place for every product delivered.

Leadership & Documentation

Support senior management by creating architecture, project management, and roadmap documentation.
Own the product lifecycle: discovery, prioritization, requirements, launch, and post-launch iteration.
Evangelize data-driven and AI-driven decision-making across the organization.
Mentor junior PMs and contribute to product process and best practices (especially at the Staff level).
Maintain a strong personal base of knowledge on data platform technology, industry practices, trends, and emerging issues.

What You'll Need

Education

Master's Degree in Statistics, Analytics, Mathematics, Economics, or a related quantitative field (preferred).

Experience

8+ years of product management experience (3+ years as a Data Analyst/similar role supporting cross-functional global business units, for candidates coming from an analytics background), with at least 2–3 years focused on data platforms, analytics, or AI/ML products.
Demonstrated experience shipping AI/ML-powered features or products (e.g., recommendation systems, predictive models, LLM-based applications, automation tools) — this is required.
Proven track record partnering closely with data engineering teams on data infrastructure, pipelines, or platform-level products.
Experience working directly with business stakeholders to translate ambiguous needs into structured product requirements.
Experience building customer-centric data products, sales-centric analytic products, and executive metrics/reporting.
Experience with data from the Customer Experience and Sales domains.
Experience in the data center domain and knowledge of data center products are nice-to-have.

Skills

Strong technical fluency: comfortable discussing data architecture, ETL/ELT pipelines, data modeling, and ML/AI concepts with engineering teams.
Strong statistical and data analysis skills, including regressions, classification, anomaly detection, and hypothesis testing, with experience applying these techniques in real analyses.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills; able to flex between technical depth and business-level storytelling.
Strong analytical skills in breaking down complex problems, processes, and systems to propose solutions.
Ability to document and prototype business use cases and data flows.
Strong quantitative skills; comfortable with SQL and interpreting data to drive decisions.
Experience with agile product development practices, roadmap planning, and prioritization frameworks.
Familiarity with the AI/ML lifecycle (data prep, model training/evaluation, deployment, monitoring) and responsible AI considerations.
Proven experience building dashboards in Tableau, Power BI, QlikView, or similar tools.
Ability to understand complex data models and connect to varied data sources such as SFDC, Exasol, Google BigQuery, and AWS.
Tableau certification is desirable, along with experience on Tableau Online (cloud), Tableau Server, and Tableau Prep.

Nice to Have

Prior experience as a data analyst, data engineer, or data scientist before transitioning into product.
Experience with generative AI / LLM-based product development.

Note - This is a business facing role we need this positionsupporting position to be remote and provide support during US hours (4:00 PM IST to 12:00 AM IST)
